title: Staged canary + fallback capacity plan for regional GPU maintenance
content:
Summary:
This working plan defines a staged canary + fallback capacity buffer for planned GPU maintenance and driver upgrades across regions. Objective is to minimize SLA impact (99th tail latency and queue depth), keep token-per-second capacity within 90% of normal for production routes, and provide a fast rollback path. This doc is intentionally conservative on headroom and prescriptive on evacuation order for multi-tenant workloads.

Scope:
- Regions: us-west-2, us-east-1, eu-west-1, asia-southeast-1
- Maintenance types: driver patch (NVIDIA driver), CUDA minor, kernel ABI tweak, host reboot, rack-level power work
- Fleet: mixed A100/V100 and some T4 pools; dedicated pools and preemptible burst nodes included

Key principles:
1) Staged canary: run driver upgrade on a small, representative subset (canary pool) per region (5–10 nodes) with synthetic workload and selected low-latency customer routes. Hold metrics 90 minutes before expanding.
2) Elastic buffer pools: pre-provision warm buffer nodes in neighboring regions (cold-warm pool) that can be activated via smart routing within 5–12 mins.
3) Job-class aware evacuation: batch/long jobs > low-priority batch > interactive low-latency routes. Prefer migrating batch first.
4) Non-disruptive fallback: if canary degrades by metric thresholds, auto-abort rollout and shift traffic to fallback pools and cross-region capacity.

Per-region capacity snapshot (pre-maintenance baseline):
- us-west-2: 240 GPUs total (150 A100, 60 V100, 30 T4). Prod-serving capacity: 180 GPUs.
- us-east-1: 300 GPUs total (180 A100, 80 V100, 40 T4). Prod-serving capacity: 230 GPUs.
- eu-west-1: 180 GPUs total (110 A100, 50 V100, 20 T4). Prod-serving capacity: 135 GPUs.
- asia-southeast-1: 120 GPUs total (60 A100, 40 V100, 20 T4). Prod-serving capacity: 95 GPUs.

Capacity buffer & fallback allocations (target):
- Canary pool per region: 5 nodes (~10 GPUs) reserved (isolated workload tag: maintenance-canary).
- Elastic buffer: keep 8% of region prod-serving capacity as warm buffer (spare images, pre-pulled weights).
- Cross-region failover agreements: us-west-2 <-> us-east-1 (primary failover), eu-west-1 can accept up to 20% extra; asia-southeast-1 limited to 10% due to network latency.

Maintenance window recommendation:
- Preferred window: 02:00–06:00 local region time on Sunday. Typical maintenance wave per region lasts 2–6 hours depending on scope.
- Example schedule (staged):
  - T0: start canary (5 nodes) + synthetic smoke tests (0–15m)
  - T1: run driver install on canary (15–40m), restart runtime, run smoke and perf suite (40–90m)
  - T2: observe metrics for stabilization window (90–150m). If OK, expand to 20% pool.
  - T3: continue staged expansion every 60m until 100% of target maintenance set completed.

Drain & evacuation order (detailed):
1) Identify nodes in maintenance set and mark as drain-candidate in Fleet API (tag: planned-maintenance-<date>).
2) Evacuate batch slots first: drain tasks labelled batch, checkpoint state, allow 30m graceful shutdown.
3) Evacuate low-priority interactive jobs next, with routing to warm buffer in-region if available.
4) Evacuate high-priority real-time routes only when necessary; prefer redirecting to cross-region pool rather than local interruption.
5) After node empty, run host pre-checks and snapshot ephemeral cache (if allowed).

Canary metrics and abort thresholds (monitored during stabilization window):
- 99th latency increase > 20% absolute over baseline -> FAIL
- Median latency increase > 35% and tail stable -> WARN (investigate)
- Queue depth (requests queued) increase > 30% -> FAIL
- Error rate (5xx) increase > 1.0 percentage point -> FAIL
- GPU OOMs or driver crashes (any occurrence) -> immediate FAIL and rollback

Alerting and dashboards:
- Canary dashboard: per-node GPU utilization, token/sec, avg/p95/p99 latency, queue_length, error_rate.
- Pager: on FAIL thresholds alert infra-sre + on-call eng-serving-runtime.

Rollback procedure (fast path):
1) Abort rollout via orchestration API: set rollout-state=aborted.
2) Re-route traffic from maintenance set to buffer nodes and cross-region pools (policy: prefer same hardware type).
3) For canary nodes: re-install previous driver artifact, reboot, rejoin pool. Confirm health checks for 30m.
4) Open incident bridge and run postmortem checklist.

Commands (examples):
- Mark node drain: curl -X POST https://fleet.redwood.internal/nodes/<node-id>/drain -d '{"reason":"driver-upgrade-2026-03-xx"}'
- Abort rollout: curl -X POST https://orchestration/api/rollouts/<rollout-id>/abort
- Promote buffer: curl -X POST https://orchestration/api/pools/activate -d '{"pool":"warm-buffer-us-west-2","scale":30}'

Network & data considerations:
- Cross-region failover only used for stateless inference routes. Stateful/kv-cache-backed routes must be pinned or have cache replication enabled.
- We will pre-warm KV caches on buffer nodes for top 20 prompt prefixes to reduce cold-start penalties.

Communication plan:
- 48h pre-notice to internal channels: #infra-maintenance, #prod-ops; include expected capacity impact and time window.
- 4h notice: targeted email to customers with Dedicated contracts > 50k/month and any customers in impacted regions with manual failover controls.
- During maintenance: live updates in #infra-maintenance; post-incident note + preliminary postmortem within 24h.

Risk matrix (top items):
- Driver incompatibility with internal runtime -> mitigated by canary and perf suite.
- Hot cache miss spike when shifting to buffer -> mitigate by pre-warm and prefix caching.
- Cross-region bandwidth saturation -> enforce route weights and throttle background syncs.

Cost impact estimate (rough):
- Activating warm buffer (8% across regions) ~ extra 45 GPUs spun up for 4 hours -> estimated cloud cost delta $3.5k – $5k depending on spot vs reserved mix.
- Customer SLA credits potential if sustained tail-latency violations >2 hours — estimated exposure per event depends on committed monthly uptime.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Confirm rollback artifact location and signed checksum for each driver build (owner: Jordan).
- Validate warm-buffer images include latest model artifacts for top-10 routes (owner: Sofia).
- Run a full rehearsal with synthetic traffic two weeks before the planned window (owner: Liam).

Appendix - quick checklist for maintenance lead:
- [ ] Confirm canary nodes selected and isolated
- [ ] Upload driver artifacts and checksums to signed storage
- [ ] Reserve warm buffer capacity and pre-pull images
- [ ] Create rollback playbook and ensure REST endpoints are reachable
- [ ] Schedule incident bridge and on-call rosters
- [ ] Publish internal & customer notices

Notes to reviewer:
This is a working doc — please comment with any region-specific constraints (legal egress, data residency), and flag contracts that require explicit customer opt-in for cross-region failover. We should avoid using asia-southeast-1 as a fallback for EU customers unless consent is documented.
